businessVision: ProjectOS delivers ordinary technical work on real projects end to end: Claude implements, the ChatGPT gatekeeper reviews through the trusted broker without the owner's relay, and ProjectOS carries each approved phase through checks, review, commit, push and closure; where the owner has delegated the closure commit to ProjectOS, a phase closes with no owner act at all, and the owner holds every protected action.
definitionOfComplete: Nine phases are complete: the temporary pieces created for the live proofs are retired and spending is disabled once the key is revoked (PROJECTOS-COMPLETION1A); and before it: one `projectos continue` carries a phase from work to closed, a phase that changes its own required validator is judged by that new copy as well as the base copy, and a third agency phase proves both with no owner act; and before them: phase write grants come from a structured list of paths in the approved plan, with the judging validators run from the last approved commit; phase closure works for any governed project; the ChatGPT gatekeeper answers without the owner's relay through the trusted broker (owner decision of 2026-10-25); ProjectOS has carried one ordinary phase end to end on a new governed project, the website of an SEO and social-media posting agency, with evidence; a project whose owner grants the closure-decision-commit scope has its delegate's closure decision committed by ProjectOS itself, with a model-invented decision time refused; and a second agency phase has closed end to end with no owner act. Dead Aisle and PolyGo are not part of this plan (owner decision of 2026-10-25). Host-attested unattended review, the signed installer, Forge and the Control Center redesign are deferred and are reopened only by an owner decision.
successStandard: On the agency project, once the owner has granted the closure-decision-commit scope, a phase runs from continue to closed with no owner act: the ChatGPT gatekeeper answers through the trusted broker, ChatGPT decides closure, and ProjectOS commits that decision and the records around it, truthfully recorded, with no protected action taken without the owner.
approvedScope: A structured per-phase list of write paths in the plan schema, the plan source format and the plan engine, from which the worker's write grant is derived exactly.
Running a phase's required validators and the loop's enforcement code from the last approved commit, so work under review cannot alter what judges it.
Generalising the closure eligibility gate from the project id 'projectos' to the governed project's own id.

Folding the run's own records into the loop's technical-continuation commit, and committing generated closure-tail records as a technical action when the phase's owner gates leave commit and push delegated.

Live proofs: the disposable two-phase proof re-run with the reduced owner acts, then one ordinary phase on a new local governed project — the website of an SEO and social-media posting agency — through projectos continue, with evidence under docs/finish/.
Tests and evidence for those live proofs; enforcement-code fixes they expose go to a separate owner-gated amendment.

By owner decision of 2026-10-25 ("Route 2 now"): the ChatGPT gatekeeper answers without the owner's relay through the existing trusted installation broker, which resolves the OpenAI key inside itself from the installation's Windows credential store, only for an allowlisted project carrying its own committed secrets-handling receipt; the agent process never holds the key.

By owner decision of 2026-10-26 ("I have given you full authority", in answer to the proposal to remove the owner's closure commit for delegated projects): a new owner-granted delegation scope, closure-decision-commit. When a project's committed closure delegation carries it and the phase leaves commit and push delegated, ProjectOS commits and pushes the delegate's closure decision and its spend ledger entry under the ProjectOS implementer identity, closes through the existing delegated phase advance, and commits the records that persist the close. A project without the scope keeps the owner's closure commit unchanged.
Refusing a closure answer whose decidedAt is not a valid timestamp inside the window of the question it answers.
A second agency phase, carried end to end under the new scope, as the live proof.
One `projectos continue` carries a phase through closure preparation into the closure question, instead of stopping after preparation (EXTERNAL-PROOF2A D7).
A phase whose write grant covers one of its own required validators is judged by the phase's copy of that validator as well as the base copy, both required to pass (EXTERNAL-PROOF2A D8).
A third agency phase, fixing the gaps in its site validator, carried with one continue and no owner act, as the live proof.

By the owner's approval of the completion delta in Plan Mode (2026-10-28): retire the temporary seo-agency installation allowlist entry, update its validator pin, disable the agency gatekeeper, and record ProjectOS's completion.
excludedScope: A second orchestrator, decision store, work queue, execution engine or gatekeeper.

Any change to the absolute owner-only actions: secrets handling and payment or live charge stay exactly as they are, and phase closure by the owner stays the default; the closure commit passes to ProjectOS only on a project whose owner has granted the closure-decision-commit scope in its committed delegation.
Production deployment, external send, payment, refund, production database mutation and credential disclosure or rotation.

Deferred by owner decision of 2026-10-25 (Option A): Host service activation, credential provisioning, signing, unattended or paid provider review, the signed installer, Programme C (Forge) and the Control Center redesign.
Deferred: live specialist engines and workforce activation, and the carried workforce deferrals recorded in plan v1.8.
Deferred to after ProjectOS completion by the owner's recorded statement: credential or token rotation where genuinely required.
Carried LOW items, each with its trigger: configuration argv forms beyond --allowedTools; hard links and device names beneath granted directories; process-tree termination on a check timeout.

By owner decision of 2026-10-25: Dead Aisle and PolyGo as proof projects; publishing to any real social-media account, sending any email or message, buying or pointing a domain, deploying the website, and creating a GitHub repository for the new project. Installing any vendored toolkit into the owner's Claude Code configuration is also excluded.
Claude creating, reading, printing, storing or relaying the OpenAI key: the owner stores it through the hidden credential prompt; the key never enters a file, command line, report or prompt.

phases.title: ProjectOS commits a delegated closure decision itself, and refuses an invented decision time
phases.description: Add the owner-granted delegation scope closure-decision-commit. When a governed project's committed closure delegation carries it and the phase's owner gates leave commit and push delegated, closure request commits and pushes exactly the closure bundle (the delegate's decision and the spend ledger) under the ProjectOS implementer identity, closure resume accepts exactly that identity for that project instead of the owner's, the phase closes through the existing delegated phase advance, and the records that persist the close are committed and pushed by ProjectOS. A project without the scope keeps the owner's closure commit. A closure answer whose decidedAt is not a valid timestamp inside the window of the question it answers is refused. The closure prompt tells the authority the time of the question and the form decidedAt must take, and only an answer produced inside the call (the trusted broker or the Host route), never an interactive answer file, is committed by ProjectOS under the grant.
